newsitem.title: USA: Nevada Power in agreement to cut rates.
newsitem.headline: Nevada Power in agreement to cut rates.

text.p: Nevada Power Co said Thursday it reached agreement with its large customers as well as the staff of the state's Public Service Commission and Office of Consumer Advocate to reduce rates by nearly $45 million.
The proposal must also be approved by the Public Service Commission itself.

Nevada Power said Las Vegas Valley residents, who will see the smallest rate cut of all customer classes, would also benefit indirectly from the lower rates since public entities would receive the largest rate reduction.

The utility noted the decrease results from its ability to take advantage of low prices for purchased power in wholesale markets, lower overall fuel costs, and other efficiency improvements in the last year.

If approved by the commission, public entities such as the Southern Nevada Water Authority, Las Vegas Valley cities and the Clark County School District would receive $11 million in annual rate reductions. Medium-sized commercial customers and other large customers would receive a $27 million rate reduction.
Residential customers and small commercial customers would see a reduction of $7 million.
Since the fall of 1994, Nevada Power said it will have reduced rates by more than $88 million overall, or more than 10 percent over a two-year period.
